what_it_does: Estimating how much power a chip design will consume normally requires finishing the full physical layout of the chip and then running expensive commercial simulation software — a slow process that happens too late in the design cycle to easily steer decisions. ATLAS tackles this by predicting final, cycle-by-cycle power consumption starting from an early-stage description of the circuit (a gate-level netlist — essentially a logical blueprint before any physical placement is done). It uses a machine learning approach with two training phases: first, a self-supervised pre-training step that teaches the model about circuit structure without needing labeled examples, then a fine-tuning step aimed at matching the power numbers a commercial simulator would produce. The model handles the three main sources of chip power — the clock distribution network, registers (flip-flops that hold state), and the logic gates in between — separately, which lets it produce fine-grained time-varying power estimates much earlier in the design flow.
